item.title: Settling down: Nvidia Growth and the Meta Settlement
item.description:
Meta agreed to an $18 billion settlement...
Duck! Yesterday, in the small town of Buñol, Spain, thousands of people gathered to be left on red. The revelers attended the town’s annual tomato-flinging food fight, a tradition dating back to 1945 and now attended by international tourists, subject to only one rule: squash the tomatoes before you toss them. This year’s event included 165 tons of tomatoes. While the world’s biggest food fight leaves behind an epic mess , don’t feel bad for the town: Because of the citric acid contained in the tomatoes strewn everywhere, the cleanup leaves Buñol more sparkling than it was before.
https://www.morningbrew.com/issues/settling-down

item.title: Supersized sanctions: Why the world is choosing friction
item.description:
The US threatened a crackdown on Iran's trading partners...
Hello there. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is facing criticism for seldom leaving her official residence on weekends or holidays. She has responded that it’s actually efficient and reduces the burden on her staff, since she has a WFH setup there. She also mentioned that although she isn’t interacting with the public on those days, she is sharing her space with cockroaches. Or she was, until her staff spread poison—at which point she was “relieved, but somehow also felt a little lonely.” Ok, we have no comment on the politics here, but if she’s befriending the roaches, she probably should get out more.
https://www.morningbrew.com/issues/supersized-sanctions

item.description:
The trade war is escalating with our northern neighbor...
Cough, cough. Feeling a little bit under the weather? You’re not alone. Today, Aug. 24, is the most popular day of the year for US employees to call out sick, according to a survey by PTO management software company Flamingo. It even tops America’s second-sickest day of the year, Feb. 13—which suspiciously usually lines up with the day after the Super Bowl. So, if this is because there was a big party last night, can someone please toss us an invite next time?

item.title: Sweaty Startup Brew: Why Boring Businesses Are Making Millions
item.description:
Get your hands dirty...
Good morning. That landscaping business you and your friends tried to start in high school before realizing it required time and energy you preferred to spend on video games wasn’t a half-bad idea. Turns out, that’s all the rage these days. Welcome to Sweaty Startup Brew, a special edition on the movement devoted to starting “boring” and often physically demanding businesses (as opposed to VC-backed tech companies). The next million-dollar powerwashing success story may be waiting at the other end of this newsletter.

item.title: Going after ghosts: Ghost Jobs and the Broken Economic Map
item.description:
Lawmakers are targeting ghost jobs...
Good morning, and many happy returns to the world’s oldest living person, Ethel Caterham, who turned 117 yesterday. Caterham once attributed her longevity to her agreeable demeanor, telling the Associated Press, her secret was “never arguing with anyone.” It’s way too late for us to try that, so I guess we’ll have to stick with eating right and getting enough sleep for long enough that Bryan Johnson figures out how to make us immortal.
